summary: Players take turns picking up meeples from a shared board in a Mancala-like sowing action, capturing the last-dropped-on square and its tribe for various effects, then sending their Djinn/Elder meeples off to score at game end. It's a tense spatial puzzle where good squares get sniped constantly and the board shrinks as tiles and camels are removed.
praised: tight, tense turn order with lots of blocking
high player interaction without direct conflict
quick to teach relative to its depth
criticised: can have significant downtime as the board narrows late game
strong 'take that' feel can frustrate newer players
some combos (assassins, viziers) can feel swingy or snowbally
two-player feels quite different/less interactive than 3-4

interaction.kind: blocking, denial, and direct meeple/tile removal

scoring.why: points come from tribe combos, resources, gold, and end-game bonus cards, so the winner is whoever chains the most efficient multi-source engine

_name: Five Tribes: The Djinns of Naqala
